entries.mechanism: UKMOD's Pension Credit take-up / Universal-Credit-transition correction (take-up estimate $PCGCSCTU = 0.69, applied through the stochastic i_rand_tu draw and the i_bsa_noUC / i_bsa_yesUC split inside bsa_uk) marks this hypothetical single pensioner (reached state pension age, no assessable income) as a non-taker / transitioned to Universal Credit and returns a zero Pension Credit award. The Axiom pipeline computes the full single standard minimum guarantee of 238.00/week, which UKMOD pays whenever this unit draws take-up. Switching the random_uk policy off does not suppress the draw (verified — results identical), and the draw is stochastic per row rather than composition-determined (verified by batch-size-1 and identical-copy runs; see suite header), so this is a UKMOD modelling behaviour for hypothetical benefit units, not an Axiom encoding gap.

UKMOD returns a zero Pension Credit award for this single pensioner with 6,000/year of state pension (assessed as boact_s 500.00/month = 115.07/ week) because of the stochastic take-up / Universal-Credit-transition draw. The Axiom guarantee credit is the single standard minimum guarantee less the assessed weekly state pension: 238.00 - 115.068493 = 122.931507/week, which UKMOD pays whenever this unit draws take-up. The zero is a draw, not the income test: at --comparison-batch-size 1 every case in the suite zeros, and identical copies of an entitled household in one run receive different awards purely by position (see the suite header and euromod_issues.json#ukmod-pc-boamt-takeup-transition).

Switching random_uk off does not suppress the draw, and the draw is stochastic per row (verified by batch-size-1 and identical-copy runs; see suite header), so the zero is a UKMOD modelling behaviour, not an Axiom encoding gap.
